short_description: Run Xposed-API modules on a stock, non-rooted Android device via Shizuku.
detailed_description:
ShizuPosed is an Xposed-compatible hook framework that runs on a locked bootloader, without root, and without repackaging APKs. It uses Shizuku to launch a target app under its own control via app_process, then installs ART hooks from inside that same process.

**What it does:**
- Runs standard Xposed-API modules inside target apps
- Works on Android 10+ without root or bootloader unlock
- Installs hooks during the target's bootstrap, before Application.onCreate
- Ships XStealth, a built-in privacy module for hiding from detection checks

**What it isn't:**
- Not LSPosed. ShizuPosed is a per-launch hook framework, not system-wide injection.
- The target app has to be launched from ShizuPosed for hooks to install.
- system_server and zygote-wide hooking are not reachable.

If you need zygote-wide coverage or system_server hooks, use LSPosed. If you can't or won't root, ShizuPosed is for you.
developer_message: Built for people who can't root or won't. If a module doesn't work, check the compatibility notes on XDA before reporting it as broken — many modules need system_server or zygote coverage, and that's a structural limit, not a bug.

build_variants.name: Standard
build_variants.description: Normal build. Package name com.shizuposed.manager. Updates like any other app.

build_variants.name: Stealth
build_variants.description: Separate build with a scrambled package name. Launcher label is 'Sync Service'. Cannot update the standard build; switching between them requires uninstalling one and installing the other.

modules.name: Sysku ADB Module
modules.description: Optional ADB-side helper for Sysku, the syscall-level interposer. Provides the heartbeat loop and service.sh that let libsysku.so run in full mode. Install only if you have enabled Sysku in the manager and the manager reports 'Enabled (module not running)'.
